name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
description: The single-leg calf raise places the entire bodyweight on one calf at a time, dramatically increasing the load relative to the bilateral standing calf raise without requiring additional equipment. The greater per-leg load also facilitates a larger range of motion and addresses left-right strength imbalances. It is an effective and equipment-free progression for gastrocnemius and soleus development.

execution.starting_position: Stand with one foot on the edge of a step, the other leg lifted slightly with knee bent. Hold onto a support with one hand for balance.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a stair, step, or raised plate for a heel drop. Hold a wall or rack lightly for balance. Dumbbell can be held in the same-side hand to increase load.
steps: Step 1: Stand on one foot on the edge of a step. Keep the other foot lifted off the floor.
Step 2: Lower the heel as far below the step as possible — full gastrocnemius stretch.
Step 3: Rise to the highest possible plantarflexion, pressing through the big toe.
Step 4: Hold the peak contraction for one second.
Step 5: Lower under control. Complete all reps then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you rise. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Rising through the outer edge of the foot rather than through the big toe
Not allowing a full heel drop at the bottom
Moving too fast — the calf responds well to slow, full-range reps
safety_considerations: If balance is challenging, hold the support more firmly initially
Start with bodyweight before progressing to a weighted dumbbell
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximum heel drop at the bottom; maximum plantar-flexion at the top.
coaching_cues: Press through the big toe — not the pinky
Drop the heel all the way
Full contraction at the top — don't cut it short
